title: BEFORE THE LORD, IN FRONT OF THE ALTAR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"These are the regulations for the grain offering: Aaron's sons are to bring it before the LORD, in front of the altar. The priest is to take a handful of the finest flour and some olive oil, together with all the incense on the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as an aroma pleasing to the LORD."'" - Lev 6:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The instructions turn now to the priests. Chapter 2 told the worshipper what to bring; chapter 6 tells the priest what to do with it.

That is worth noticing. God gave detailed instructions to both sides. The person offering needed to know how to give, and the person receiving needed to know how to handle it.

There is wisdom here for anyone who receives what others give — pastors, church treasurers, leaders of any ministry. What people place in your hands was brought before the LORD. It is not merely resources; it is somebody's worship. Handling it carelessly is not just poor administration. It is mishandling something holy.

Paul was scrupulous about this. Writing about a financial gift he was carrying, he said he was taking pains to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord but also in the eyes of man (2 Cor 8:21). He deliberately involved others so that no one could question his integrity.

And notice again the phrase that keeps returning: an aroma pleasing to the LORD. The priest's careful, correct handling of the offering is part of what makes it pleasing.

How we treat what people entrust to us matters to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has been entrusted to me by others, and am I handling it carefully?
2. Do I treat other people's giving and service as something holy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me trustworthy with whatever others place in my hands. Let me handle their offerings as reverently as I would want mine handled. Amen.
